objective: Separate concurrency and speculative-token effects for three long-IO random workloads using matched BF16 and FP8 runs.
summary: All 72 runs completed. FP8 was slower in only 1/36 matched cells. Concurrency had a larger marginal effect than spec depth on absolute throughput, while their interaction remained substantial.
next_actions: Repeat boundary cells to quantify run-to-run variance.
Replay an anonymized real agent trace with tool-call timing.
Evaluate adaptive speculative depth against fixed s4, s8, and s16.
